# SPD-037 — Bash hook cd success proxy: cd into an existing-but-unenterable dir escapes redirection checks

## Brief
SPD-030's directory model marks a cd 'uncertain' (keeps both old and new dir) only when the target is missing (os.path.isdir False). A directory that exists but the process cannot chdir into (no execute bit, e.g. /var/root, or a dir a member itself chmod 000's) passes isdir, so the hook assumes the cd succeeded and checks a relative redirection only against the target dir. The real shell's cd fails, the shell stays put, and with ; or || continuation the write lands in the original (repo) directory unchecked. Using os.access(d, os.X_OK) instead of (or with) os.path.isdir in the cd_uncertain check in directory_change would keep both directories and refuse. Narrow: the && form is already safe (the write does not run); git writes after such a cd are still caught; unchanged from origin/main, so not a regression.

Evidence: Probe (zsh 5.9, bash 3.2): 'cd /var/root' -> 'permission denied', PWD stays /tmp in both. Differential rig, member with deliverable ** and with tests/**: 'cd /var/root; echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md' is SILENT on both origin/main and the branch, though the real write is <cwd>/ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md inside the repo. os.path.isdir('/var/root')=True while os.access('/var/root', os.X_OK)=False. Same class as the broader pre-existing gap that the Bash redirect/tee net does not model writes by arbitrary programs (cp, python -c open(), sed -i, dd), which are also SILENT on both; the render-conflict detection and the Edit-tool hook are the real guardrails.

## Size, persona and model decision
Batch plan v2, wave 3 with SPD-049, SPD-045 and SPD-035, same engineer on opus. Wholly inside directory_change in shell/directories.py: os.access(d, os.X_OK) beside os.path.isdir in the uncertain check.
